parameters.description: Its parameters side by side, when both runs use one camera model.

projection.description: Where the two calibrations project the same rays.

CameraEvidence.description:
One camera's fit in one run. The residual statistics are in-sample:
they compare like with like only between runs of the same observations.

max_projection_sigma_px.description:
The largest major-axis projection σ over a grid across the image,
pixels; `None` without a covariance of the camera's parameters.

model.description:
Its model; `None` for a general sensor homography, which no model
spec describes.

reprojection.description:
The statistics of its reprojection error lengths (mean, RMS, median,
95th percentile, largest), pixels; `None` without projected features.

unprojected.description: Features the calibrated camera could not project.

views.description: The views it observed features in.

CameraModelSpec.description:
A camera model: the kind in each slot. The values live in
[`CameraParams`](super::CameraParams); [`CameraParams::spec`](super::CameraParams::spec)
recovers the spec from them.

Compensation.description:
How the second camera's frame is aligned with the first's before their
projections are compared.

oneOf.description:
Compare the rays as the two calibrations place them, without
re-orienting either camera: for a camera frame used as calibrated,
such as one run's intrinsics combined with another run's extrinsics.

Fit the rotation of the second camera's frame that brings its
projections closest to the first's (the default). The orientation of
a camera frame is not separately observable from what uses the
camera, so the difference left is the part no re-orientation removes.

ConfigChange.description: One setting where two configurations differ.

other.description: The other run's value as JSON text; `None` where it has none.

path.description:
The setting, as a path into the configuration's JSON
(`config.optimize.reprojection_loss`, `config.camera.fix[2]`).

reference.description: The reference's value as JSON text; `None` where it has none.

CovarianceStatus.description: Whether a run has a covariance of its estimates.

oneOf.description: It has one.

shared_parameters.description: The number of shared (not per-view) parameters it covers.

view_scatter.description:
The factor the covariance was scaled by because the views
scatter more than the residual noise predicts; `None` when it
was not scaled.

oneOf.description: It has none, for the reason given.

DataRelation.description:
How the observations of a run relate to the reference run's: what
decides which test of a difference is valid.

oneOf.description: Not established: no test.
No observation in common: independent captures of the device.
The same observations and the same configuration.

The same observations under another configuration (camera model,
loss, solver).

One run's observations are a strict subset of the other's, and the
configurations are equal: the runs differ by what was left out.

Shared and differing observations, or nested observations under
different configurations.

DifferenceTest.description: The test of a scalar difference `Δ = other − reference`.

oneOf.description:
Independent captures: `σ_Δ = √(σ_ref² + σ_other²)`, `z = Δ / σ_Δ`.
Under the hypothesis that both runs estimate the same value, `z` is
standard normal.

Nested observations under one configuration:
`σ_Δ = √(σ_smaller² − σ_larger²)` (the Hausman form, each variance
taken at the larger run's view-scatter factor), `z = Δ / σ_Δ`. Under
the hypothesis that the left-out observations fit the model as the
others do, `z` is standard normal.
No valid test.

DistortionKind.description:
Which distortion model a camera carries.

`dim() == 0` means the camera has no distortion parameter block.

oneOf.description: No distortion; no parameter block.
Brown-Conrady `[k1, k2, k3, p1, p2]`.
Rational polynomial `[k1, k2, k3, k4, k5, k6, p1, p2]`.
Brown-Conrady + thin-prism `[k1, k2, k3, p1, p2, s1, s2, s3, s4]`.
Fitzgibbon division model `[lambda]`.

Kannala-Brandt radial polynomial `[k1, k2, k3, k4]`; with
[`ProjectionKind::Equidistant`] the Kannala-Brandt fisheye model.

NoTest.description: Why a difference has no test.

oneOf.description: The data relation is not known.
The runs have the same observations and configuration.

The runs share observations ([`DataRelation::SameData`],
[`DataRelation::Overlapping`]): their errors are correlated by an
amount neither export states.
A run has no covariance.
A run held the quantity fixed, so states no σ of it.

Nested runs whose stated variances do not order (the smaller run's
variance is not the larger): the Hausman form has no σ.

The runs' rigs have different reference cameras, so the other run's
covariance is not of the compared pose.
The covariance of the difference is singular.

ParameterComparison.description: A camera's parameters in two runs.

oneOf.description: Both runs use one model: each parameter, in the solver's order.

The models differ, so a parameter of one is not a parameter of the
other; the projection difference compares them.

A camera whose parameters the solver does not name (a general
sensor homography).

delta_over_reference_sigma.description:
`delta / reference_sigma`, signed: whether the change matters at
the precision the reference claims. Not a test: two runs of the same
observations can differ by many σ of either without disagreeing, and
by a fraction of one while disagreeing.

label.description:
The parameter, as the covariance labels it without its camera
prefix (`fx`, `k1`, `tilt_x`).

other.description: Its value in the other run.

other_sigma.description: The other run's stated σ, likewise.

reference_sigma.description:
The reference's stated σ; `None` when it did not estimate the
parameter or has no covariance.

test.description: The test of the difference, when the data relation supports one.

PlaneDifference.description: A camera's laser plane in two runs, in the camera's frame.

distance_other_m.description:
The other run's distance, its plane's sign matched to the
reference's normal, metres.

distance_over_reference_sigma.description: `distance_delta_m` over the reference's σ of `d`. Not a test.

distance_reference_m.description: The reference's distance `d` of `n · p + d = 0`, metres.

distance_test.description:
The test of the distance difference, when the data relation
supports one.

normal_angle_deg.description: The angle between the two normals, degrees.

delta_over_reference_sigma.description:
The tangent's length in the reference's covariance,
`√(τᵀ Σ_ref⁻¹ τ)`: the change in units of the reference's stated
uncertainty. Not a test.

label.description:
The pose, its frames named by camera id: `<camera>_se3_<reference>`
for a camera's pose relative to the reference run's reference
camera; `gripper_se3_<reference>` or `<reference>_se3_base` for the
hand-eye.

rotation_deg.description: The angle of the rotation between the two, degrees.

tangent.description:
`Log(P_ref⁻¹ · P_other)` as `[ωx, ωy, ωz, vx, vy, vz]` (radians,
metres): the difference in the covariance's right-perturbation
tangent, in the pose's source frame.

test.description: The test of the difference, when the data relation supports one.

translation_m.description:
The translations' difference, `other − reference`, in the pose's
target frame, metres.

PoseTest.description:
The test of a pose difference, its tangent `τ` against the covariance
of the difference.

oneOf.description: Independent captures: `χ² = τᵀ (Σ_ref + Σ_other)⁻¹ τ`.

Nested observations under one configuration:
`χ² = τᵀ (Σ_smaller − Σ_larger)⁻¹ τ` (the Hausman form).
No valid test.

ProblemKind.description:
The calibration problem a dataset is for, and the kind of an export.

One value per problem type, serialized as its snake_case name
(`"planar_intrinsics"`, …). A manifest names it in its `topology` field,
which selects the problem a run dispatches to; every export carries it in
its `kind` field, so a consumer narrows on one value instead of probing
which fields are present. The tag is required on deserialize.

A problem kind describes the data (how many cameras, robot poses, laser
images), not the camera model: a tilted (Scheimpflug) single camera is a
`planar_intrinsics` dataset whose calibration config names the sensor.

oneOf.description:
Single camera, planar target — `PlanarIntrinsicsProblem` (any camera
model, including a tilted sensor).
Single camera mounted on a robot — `SingleCamHandeyeProblem`.
Camera + laser plane — `LaserlineDeviceProblem`.
Multi-camera rig, target only — `RigExtrinsicsProblem`.
Multi-camera rig + robot — `RigHandeyeProblem`.
Multi-camera rig + robot + laser planes — joint hand-eye/laser BA.
Multi-camera rig + laser planes — `RigLaserlineDeviceProblem`.

ProjectionComparison.description: Where two calibrations of a camera project the same rays.

oneOf.description:
The projection difference, `other − reference` at the reference's
rays, after the compensation; fitted on the grid blocks either run's
features cover.

compensation.description: How the other camera's frame was aligned.

fit_nodes.description:
Grid nodes the rotation was fitted on and the `*_fit_px`
statistics are taken over: the covered region.

max_fit_px.description: The largest difference over the fitted nodes, pixels.

max_valid_px.description: The largest difference over every valid node, pixels.

rms_fit_px.description: The root mean square difference over the fitted nodes, pixels.

rms_valid_px.description:
The root mean square over every valid node, pixels: outside the
covered region, an extrapolation of both models.

rotation_deg.description: The angle of the compensating rotation, degrees.

valid_nodes.description: Grid nodes where both cameras have a value.

oneOf.description: Not computed, for the reason given.

ProjectionKind.description: Which projection model a camera uses.

oneOf.description: Pinhole (perspective) projection; no parameters of its own.

Equidistant (fisheye) projection: radius = incidence angle, in
radians; no parameters of its own. With
[`DistortionKind::KannalaBrandt4`] it is the Kannala-Brandt fisheye
model.

ReprojectionStats.description:
Summary statistics for reprojection errors.

The percentiles (`median`, `p95`) interpolate linearly between order
statistics of the ascending-sorted errors, the default of numpy and
pandas: the `q`-quantile of `n` errors lies at fractional rank
`q * (n - 1)`, so the median of an even count is the mean of the middle
two. They are present when the statistics were computed from the errors
([`from_errors`](Self::from_errors)), and absent when built from
aggregates ([`from_summary`](Self::from_summary)).

median.description:
Median reprojection error in pixels (the 50th percentile, linearly
interpolated); `None` when built from aggregates. `0.0` for no
errors, as the other statistics.

p95.description:
95th percentile of the reprojection error in pixels, linearly
interpolated; `None` when built from aggregates.

rms.description: Root mean square error in pixels.

cameras.description: Each camera both runs have, in the reference's camera order.

config_changes.description:
Where the two configurations differ; `None` when either run's
configuration was not given.

fit_comparable.description:
Whether the two runs' in-sample residual statistics compare like
with like: only for the same observations ([`DataRelation::Identical`],
[`DataRelation::SameData`]). A run that left out its worst features
always has a lower residual, which says nothing of its calibration.

handeye.description:
The hand-eye, expressed for the reference run's reference camera;
`None` unless both runs calibrated one in the same mode.

laser_planes.description: Each camera's laser plane, for the cameras both runs have one for.

model_changes.description: The cameras, by id, whose camera models differ between the runs.

relation.description: How its observations relate to the reference's, as stated.

rig.description:
Each camera's pose relative to the reference run's reference camera,
for the cameras both runs have (a rig).

run.description:
The run's position in the comparison (1 for the first run after the
reference).

unmatched_cameras.description:
The cameras of the run the reference does not have, and the
reference's cameras it does not have, by id.

RunEvidence.description:
One run's own evidence: its quality verdict, its covariance and the fit
of each camera.

cameras.description: Each camera, in the run's camera order.

reference_camera.description:
The camera whose frame is the rig frame (its pose in the rig is the
identity), by id; for one camera, that camera.

verdict.description: Its quality verdict, judged by the options' thresholds.

RunSide.description: One of the two runs of a difference.

oneOf.description: The reference run, the first of the comparison.
The run compared with it.

SensorKind.description: Which sensor model a camera uses.

oneOf.description: Sensor plane perpendicular to the optical axis; no parameters.
Scheimpflug tilted sensor `[tilt_x, tilt_y]` (radians).

UncertaintyUnavailable.description: Why a result has no covariance.

oneOf.description: The solve stopped on its iteration budget, short of a minimum.

The data does not determine these parameters (or combinations of
them): too few or too similar views, or a free gauge.

These parameters ended on a bound, where a Gaussian covariance does
not describe them.

labels.description: Labels of the parameters on a bound.

oneOf.description: No more observations than estimated parameters.
The result was produced or stored without uncertainty.

The result depends on a calibration that has no covariance, or none
for the cameras it uses (a laser calibration that held the cameras'
intrinsics fixed), so a covariance from the result's own observations
would leave out the calibration's share.

Verdict.description:
The judgment of a result, or of one check.

Ordered by severity: `Pass < Warn < Fail`.

oneOf.description: Nothing found that limits the result.
Usable, with a weakness worth knowing; the message says which.
The data does not support the result.

description:
Runs side by side against the first, the reference: what
[`compare_runs`] returns.

differences.description: Each run after the first against the reference, in run order.

runs.description:
What each run says of itself, in the given order; the first is the
reference.
